name: True Unicornuate Uterus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Classification

criteria.description: Presence of a single developed uterine horn with absence or hypoplasia of the contralateral horn
Confirmation of uterine morphology by imaging modalities such as MRI or 3D ultrasound
Absence or hypoplasia of the fallopian tube on the side of the absent uterine horn

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a single developed uterine horn confirmed by imaging with absent or hypoplastic contralateral horn
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from other Mullerian anomalies is essential for accurate diagnosis.

searchTerms: single uterine horn seen on scan

common.notes: Due to reduced uterine volume and abnormal endometrium
searchTerms: loss of pregnancy in early weeks

common.notes: Increased risk due to abnormal uterine anatomy

searchTerms: pelvic pain not linked to periods
chronic pelvic pain unrelated to cycle

occasional.symptomName: Ipsilateral renal anomalies other than agenesis
searchTerms: kidney abnormalities other than missing kidney
psychological issues related to inability to conceive

imaging: MRI showing single uterine horn with absent contralateral horn
Intravenous pyelogram or renal ultrasound demonstrating ipsilateral renal agenesis or anomalies
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; considered a congenital Mullerian duct anomaly
other: Surgical findings during laparoscopy confirming unilateral uterine development

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of two uterine horns connected by a myometrial bridge
Two endometrial cavities visible on imaging
Presence of a rudimentary horn which may or may not communicate with the main uterine cavity
Possible hematometra or pain due to non-communicating horn

redFlags: Severe dysmenorrhea with non-communicating rudimentary horn
Ipsilateral renal agenesis indicating associated urinary tract anomaly
references: American Society for Reproductive Medicine. The ASRM classification of Müllerian anomalies. Fertil Steril. 2021.
Rock JA, et al. Mullerian anomalies: diagnosis and management. Obstet Gynecol Clin North Am. 2017.
